This is a blog where I dive deep into the internals of XLA Compilation, Pallas, and the whole MLIR lowering pipeline. To follow along, you only need a moderate understanding of computer architecture, a cape, and our trusty companion DMA the dog (idk how ChatGPT came up with this)!

fr:mainmatter.html:p: To understand these flags, one first needs to understand the Pallas lowering pipeline.

html:ul.html:li: Dispatch / Cache: caches compilation based on input argument signatures i.e. shapes, dtypes, sharding. If shapes change will need to recompile.
XLA transformation: Python -> JaxPR -> StableHLO, performing fusion and other simplifications to reduce memory overhead (?).
TPU specific: Further reduced to LLO IR, then very large instruction word (VLIW) scheduling to map dot products to MXU.

fr:mainmatter.html:div: Remark. As soon as python code is traced into jaxpr it is thrown away. Only HLO is input to XLA compiler.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: We have the following compilation pipeline

html:ul.html:li: Abstract execution. JAX executes python code using abstract tracer objects instead of real arrays.
Every operation and its intermediate result is recorded into jaxpr.
Sequence used to construct a grap, which the XLA compiler will later optimize.
Python code is executed once during tracing but excluded from final graph.
Each JAX primitive registers functions for
Lowering to StableHLO
How it is transformed under grad and vmap.
Multiple ML frameworks lower to StableHLO.
Hardware agnostic.
Backwards compatible.

html:ol.html:li: Compile: HLO -> Optimized HLO -> LLO IR -> VLIW -> Executables

html:ul.html:li: compiled.runtime_executable() returns a LoadedExecutable.
Useful(?) compiled.cost_analysis().
HLO:
Input for XLA compiler.
Directed acyclic graph of copmutational operations.
All array dimensions are known at compile time.
Limited opcodes i.e. Add, Multiply, Transpose, Dot, etc.
Every data type defined by data type and fixed dimensions, determined at compile time.
Minor-to-major order i.e. fastest changing to slowesting changin.
Tiling: arrays are split into smaller blocks to fit into VREG. Want to arrange data to efficiently fit VREG.

html:figure.html:figcaption: How memory is laid out based on XLA.

html:ul.html:li: Move tensors from CPU to HBM. Sharding is taken care of by PJIT if on TPU pod.
Async: Immediately returns a Future JAX array while the hardware executes VLIW microcode asynchronously.
Buffer management: Returns pointer to TPU memory. All handled lazily. Not copied back to CPU until jax.block_until_ready().

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Deepseek v1 through R1: RL is back! › How is R1 different then previous iterations of models?

html:ul.html:li: In R1-Zero, they do ZERO SFT on the base model - directly apply reinforcement learning.
Use PPO like policy optimization but do NOT learn a reward model.

Use very simple reward:
+1 for correct answer
-0.5 for incorrect answer
-1 for inability to answer.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Traditional actor critic RL algorithms, require training both an actor and a critic (as the name implies). Typically, these components are both of equal size. In the field of RL, this is non-problematic because models are typically rather small (at least in comparison to LLMs). In DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

fr:tree.fr:mainmatter:
\begin {align*} {\mathcal {J}}_{\mathrm {GRPO}}(\theta )&= \mathbb {E}[q\sim P(Q),\{o_{i}\}_{i=1}^{G}\sim \pi _{\theta _{o l d}}(O|q)] \\ &= \frac {1}{G}\sum _{i=1}^{G}\left (\operatorname *{min}\left (\frac {\pi _{\theta }(o_{i}|q)}{\pi _{\theta _{o d}}(o_{i}|q)}A_{i},\operatorname *{clip}\left (\frac {\pi _{\theta }(o_{i}|q)}{\pi _{\theta _{o d d}}(o_{i}|q)},1-\varepsilon ,1+\varepsilon \right )A_{i}\right )-\beta \mathbb {D}_{K L}\left (\pi _{\theta }||\pi _{r e f}\right )\right ) \end {align*}
where
\mathbb {D}_{\mathrm {K L}}\left (\pi _{\theta }||\pi _{\mathrm {ref}}\right )=\frac {\pi _{\mathrm {ref}}(o_{i}|q)}{\pi _{\theta }(o_{i}|q)}-\log \frac {\pi _{\mathrm {ref}}(o_{i}|q)}{\pi _{\theta }(o_{i}|q)}-1
The astute RL reader will notice this is essentially PPO. The key distinction here is that the advantage A_i is not computed using a critic model. Instead, A_{i}=\frac {r_{i}-\mathrm {mean}(\{r_{1},r_{2},\cdots ,r_{G}\})}{\mathrm {std}(\{r_{1},r_{2},\cdots ,r_{G}\})}.
